questions.question_text: Which word describes what a chord (or arc) does to the angle formed at a point when its endpoints are joined to that point?

options.why: Bisects means cuts exactly in half; it does not describe forming an angle at a point.
Circumscribes describes a shape drawn around another shape, not forming an angle at a point.

questions.solution_text:
Joining the two endpoints of a chord or arc to a point forms an angle there.
The chord or arc **subtends** that angle.

options.why: The vertex must be the middle letter; this puts $Z$ first instead of in the middle.
The vertex must be the middle letter; this puts $Z$ last instead of in the middle.

questions.solution_text:
The vertex of the angle is $Z$, so it must be the middle letter.
The angle is written $\angle XZY$.
